thesis: Crafty should feel like a hand-painted toy diorama of a frontier where light is the thing you fight for: Ember against the dark. By day it is a warm, readable bold-flat world under an authored sky. By night it is a cool, moonlit siege in which every bright thing on screen means something. Either it is the player's power (the Hearth, a lantern they placed, a shrine they relit, glowing ore, a spell core, the beast form's ember) or it is a threat's tell (a mob's eyes, the red edge of a windup, the dragon's throat glow). Bloom, warmth and saturation are spent only on meaning; shadows are designed colour rather than leftover cobalt; every silhouette reads at 64 px. Play is close and legible. You cannot outwalk a fight, so you answer each telegraph with a dodge, a heavy, a string finisher or an Aspect. The climb from Hearth to Blight Heart is a chain of shrines you relight, and each one weakens the dragon. The game also runs cool on purpose: a pixel budget instead of a pixel ratio, quality tiers that settle instead of oscillating, and nothing redrawn that did not change. That keeps the M3 Max quiet and lets the iPad show the same game. The moment a player remembers is when the dark comes and they light it back.

moves.name: Steady tiers and an honest iPad
moves.what: (a) Fix the governor. After a decline from tier T, block re-inclining to T for 60 s, doubling the wait on each repeat, and keep the lower tier for the rest of the session after 2 declines. Under the frame cap, incline only when headroom is measured: FrameCap times advance() and must stay below 55% of the frame interval. Step dpr continuously first. Never change renderDistance or the far-field radius at runtime on coarse-pointer devices. Delete AdaptiveDpr, since nothing calls regress(). (b) Make the composer follow the pixel ratio: a child of EffectComposer calls composer.setSize when gl.getPixelRatio() changes. This is the local form of the react-postprocessing 3.1.3 fix. (c) Wrap GodRays and N8AO in local components that build each effect once, toggle it for horizon and tier changes, and dispose it on unmount. (d) Context loss: wire the never-read isWebGLContextLost flag to a recovery panel ('Graphics were reset by the system: tap to resume', which autosaves and reloads), and write a localStorage breadcrumb (tier, dpr, canvas px, uptime, tier changes). (e) At boot, check that a 4x4 RGBA16F target and an R32F+RGBA16F MRT are framebuffer-complete; if not, fall back to UnsignedByte buffers with N8AO off. (f) Title screen: TitleDiorama gets antialias off on coarse pointers, alpha false and NEUTRAL tone mapping, and unmounts after Start; the parked canvasPace stops the game canvas drawing behind it. (g) Instruments: a Diagnostics panel reachable by touch from Settings (UA, GL renderer, dpr, canvas px, tier timeline, context-loss breadcrumbs, framebuffer status); the untracked ipad-probe committed and run on the PROD build in WebKit at 1180x820 and 820x1180 with hasTouch; and a lookbook probe. The lookbook runs the prod build on a real GPU in Chromium and WebKit with motion on, shoots 12 hero shots each at dawn, golden hour and moonlit night plus 3 combat moments, and is published as a contact-sheet artifact at each milestone.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Kevin's iPad shows the game as 'very buggy / broken'. The source has several mechanisms that would produce that. Under the 60 fps cap the governor climbs until a tier fails and then falls back, in a loop of roughly 5 s. Each step remounts N8AO and GodRays (shader compiles on Metal), reallocates every composer target and rebuilds the shadow map. The composer stays at the old pixel ratio, which is the upstream N8AO ghosting symptom (#280). Effect render targets leak. A lost context leaves a black canvas under a live HUD with no way back. A player sees this as flicker, shimmering shadows, hitches and a dead screen. Once fixed, the iPad settles on one look and stays there.

moves.win: The iPad stops being a second-class rail. It settles on a tier within 20 s, never flickers, survives a context loss, and every claim about it rests on a frame or a screenshot from the device. The lookbook becomes the acceptance surface for every looks move after it, replacing SwiftShader capture frames.
moves.compose: Move 2's pixel budget becomes the governor's first lever, so most adaptations are a cheap dpr step rather than an effect remount. The lookbook is the lived proof for moves 4, 7, 9, 11 and 12. The later three r186 / R3F 9.8.2 / @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.2 bump replaces the local setSize and the effect wrappers with upstream equivalents (the N8AO enabled prop and EffectGroup).
moves.door: Mostly two-way: hysteresis times and the 2-decline settle are constants. The one visible surface is the Diagnostics panel; keep it under Settings > About so it stays out of the bold-flat play screen.
moves.rails: M3 Max: fewer remounts, no visual loss. iPad Safari: the target. Touch: Diagnostics needs a touch entry, because DebugOverlay opens by key only. Low tier: the framebuffer fallback protects devices where RGBA16F is not renderable. Capture mode is unaffected, since the governor is already off in capture.
moves.threat: The real iPad symptom may be something no macOS WebKit probe can reproduce, such as the Safari 26.x stacked-canvas regression or a driver bug; only Kevin's device and the breadcrumbs can see it. Hysteresis that is too sticky leaves a capable iPad on low all session. The local setSize would double-resize once the dependency upgrade lands, so delete it in that commit.

moves.name: Cool by budget
moves.what: (a) Push main so the live site gets the built-once post chain, the 60 fps cap and the shadow-size reset. (b) Pixel budget: dpr = clamp(min(cap, devicePixelRatio, sqrt(budgetPx / cssPx)), 1, cap), with high 4.2 Mpx / cap 1.75, med 2.8 / 1.5 and low 1.8 / 1.25. That is about 1.52 dpr at high in an M3 Max window, and it settles T11 by measurement instead of by taste. (c) Shadow map on demand: autoUpdate = false. Set needsUpdate when the snapped centre moves, when the sun moves more than 0.05 degrees, when a chunk inside the box mounts or remeshes, on a block edit, and at up to 30 Hz while a caster moves. Set normalBias to about 0.6 texel per tier and bias to -0.0005. Only a mob's body and head cast shadows. shadowReset must still force an update. (d) Drive the HUD from one ticker on FrameCap's rendered tick, with write-on-change throughout. Compass markers become a persistent node pool moved by translateX, replacing the parked innerHTML dedupe. (e) Pace the world at 30 fps behind opaque panels, in an unfocused window, and after 45 s idle with no hostile within 24 m. This extends the parked paceFor and never applies in capture or the perf probe. (f) Idle zeros: WeatherSystem goes invisible with no instance uploads in clear weather; SpatialAudioController writes automation only on change and runs occlusion at 15 Hz; the AudioContext is suspended while the tab is hidden. Per-frame lerps such as Components.jsx:1285 move to dt-based damping, so a steady 30 Hz (iOS Low Power Mode) is a valid cadence. (g) Instruments: a powermetrics GPU-power A/B script that Kevin runs with sudo, and per-pass timer queries in gpu-cost-probe.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Kevin's fans. At dpr 2 an M3 Max pushes about 7.7 Mpx through roughly 5 full-resolution half-float passes every frame. Four DOM requestAnimationFrame loops run at 120 Hz outside the cap, the shadow map re-renders every frame, and the world keeps rendering at 60 behind a full-screen inventory. None of that work is visible. The player gets it back as silence, battery life and no thermal throttling in the middle of a siege.

moves.win: The M3 Max runs Crafty with its fans off, and the iPad keeps headroom to spend on looks. dpr becomes a continuous lever that absorbs load before any effect is dropped.
moves.compose: With move 1, the budget and the hysteresis form one governor. The headroom freed here pays for moves 4, 9, 11 and 12 without raising the heat bill. The HUD ticker shares HUD.jsx with move 6's relayout, so do them together. Shadow-on-demand carries over to the later SunLight CSM trial.
moves.door: Two-way: every lever is a constant or a flag. The one taste call is image sharpness at about 1.5 dpr on Retina. With 32 px nearest-filtered textures and a DOM HUD that stays sharp at any canvas dpr, the side-by-side crops decide it.
moves.rails: M3 Max: the target. iPad: the budget gives 1.75 / 1.5 / 1.25 on an iPad Pro 11. Touch: TouchControlsSurface joins the ticker. Low tier: the floor is dpr 1.0 at 1.8 Mpx.
moves.threat: A softer image can read as blurry on a 5K display; react-postprocessing 3.2's Sharpness effect at low strength is the remedy once that package is upgraded. Shadow on-demand can miss an update path (a moving mob's shadow freezing); the 30 Hz caster rule and the block-edit e2e guard it. Idle pacing can show as judder if input detection misses touch or a gamepad, so idle requires no input of any kind and no hostile nearby.

moves.name: Touch plays the signature
moves.what: Make the roar sector of the Aspect ring press-and-hold. pointerdown sets the intent; pointerup, pointerleave and pointercancel clear it; setPointerCapture is used; and a radial fill shows the 0.45 s charge. The action button holds the same way: pointerdown calls pressHeavy('touch') and pointerup calls releaseHeavy, while a tap still throws the light swing at once, which heavyAttack already supports. Unify tier and touch detection on one helper (today quality.js reads pointer: coarse and touchDevice.js reads any-pointer: coarse). Add a HUD geometry invariant for iPad frames: the quest panel, minimap, pause button, joystick and action-cluster rectangles never intersect.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Reading the code, an iPad player cannot perform the Wildheart transform. The ring pulses the roar intent for 120 ms on pointer-up, while the charge needs 0.45 s and cancels the frame the intent drops. Nor can they perform the heavy attack, which is wired only to mouse button 0 and T. The game's signature moment does not exist on Kevin's second target device. After this, an iPad player gets the same game.

moves.name: Ember against the dark: the light and colour script
moves.what: Drive colour by the sun's elevation instead of the isDay boolean. Build a six-key colour script on cycleFraction (dawn pink-gold, morning, noon, golden hour, blue hour, moonlit night), with the siege and boss danger moods as overlays (a red horizon, denser fog) rather than the base night. When the sun crosses the horizon, hand the same directional light to the moon (#9DB4FF, about 0.35, on its own arc, shadows kept on), so the light count never changes. Rebalance the rig: ambient drops from 0.9 to about 0.25, and its energy moves into a desaturated hemisphere sky (#8FB4D8) with a warm ground bounce per mood. Add a shadowTint uniform in the terrain's lights_fragment_end patch beside the cloud shadow, targeting a shadow/lit luminance of about 0.55 with shadow chroma below lit chroma. Raise the bloom threshold above 1.0 and give HDR emissive only to meaningful sources (sun disc, spell cores, eyes, ore, lantern, shrine beam). Replace the global +0.30 saturation with a per-mood split-tone, in the existing HueSaturation/BrightnessContrast slot or as one Effect in the same EffectPass. Set exposure so snow and cloud tops reach about 245. Make the fog glow toward the sun (pow(dot(view, sun), 8)) and use the analytic height-fog integral. Step aerial perspective into 3-4 value planes, add a warm horizon on the sun side, fade clouds by ray distance to remove the horizon streaks, and put the moon on an arc at constant screen size.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Today the night is a sunset frozen in place: the whole night is maroon and orange with no key light (explore-night.png, opened). Shadows are saturated cobalt and teal that read as water, and bloom turns the horizon into a milky wall (explore-day.png, opened). After this, dawn and dusk become events and the night turns cool blue-violet, so every warm light reads as safety and shadows look designed. This is the move that makes any screenshot read as one authored art direction, and it costs almost nothing on the GPU.

moves.compose: The cool night is the backdrop that the parked ores, the lantern (12) and lit shrines (14) need in order to read. HDR-only bloom is the grammar move 11 uses for eyes and spell cores. The golden-hour key colours the title island (6). Water (7) takes the fog fix.

moves.rails: GPU-neutral on every rail. NEUTRAL tone mapping behaves the same in WebKit, and the title diorama moves to NEUTRAL so title and play share colour. Low tier pays nothing new: the shadow tint lives in the terrain patch, which already runs at every tier.

A moonlit night that is too dark hides the terrain, so keep the hemisphere floor. A threshold above 1 with too few HDR sources looks flat: audit that every intended glow source sets toneMapped=false and has intensity above 1.

moves.name: Close-quarters combat
moves.what: Add a combat stance in a new game/combatStance.js. The player is in combat while an aggro'd hostile is within 18 m and in line of sight, and for 2.5 s after dealing or taking damage. In combat the walk is 6.5 m/s, with backpedalling at x0.8. Out of combat the 14 m/s travel stride returns, ramped in over 0.6 s with a +4 degree FOV kick and faster footsteps. The dodge (28 to 10 m/s) becomes the real escape. Trim the melee cone from 4.5 m to 3.2 m, and raise hound and skitterling chase speed to about 6 m/s. Give each archetype a windupMs in mobArchetypes (skitterling 260, hound 320, husk 380, spider leap 450, brute 620), pass it through attackPhase, and scale the perfect-dodge window with it. Draw amber chevrons at the screen edge, from a 15 Hz reader reusing DamageDirection's perimeter math, for mobs within 8 m winding up outside the view cone. Give each archetype a spatial windup voice (a hiss, a grunt, a deep inhale). Add a 3-step light string in a new game/meleeString.js: step 3 is a 140 degree sweep at 1.5x with knockback and the heavy hitstop tier; the string resets after 650 ms; each swing slows the walk to 0.6x for 120 ms; the hand arc alternates direction.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Today the player walks at 14 m/s in every direction while chasers manage 3 to 6 m/s, so walking backwards while clicking beats every telegraph. The perfect dodge, the heavy and the brute's charge only matter to a player who chooses to stand still. After this, fights become a dance of spacing, reads and answers, and the shipped verbs (perfect dodge, heavy, stagger) finally carry weight.

moves.name: The first minute is the promise
moves.what: Re-compose the title around a living golden-hour micro-diorama built with the real terrain material and the move-4 palette: a floating island with the hut, two trees, the shrine beam, a ring of ocean and clouds. The hero stands on the left third with the staff tip glowing; the wordmark sits top-centre or right with the ink drop shadow; the call to action sits in clear space. The scrim shrinks to a band over the bottom 25%, the motes become soft additive discs, and the camera orbits at 0.02 rad/s, paced by canvasPace. Rewrite the tagline around the real promise (four Aspects, a frontier, a dragon) and move it into i18n; today it is a hardcoded English string. Then build the Ember Prologue, 60-90 s and once per profile, with a skip. At spawn the siege horn sounds and a scripted wave of 2 husks and a brute comes from a compass-marked bearing (spawnMob already takes a forced type). Old Pike's line teaches dodge. When the brute winds up, the game grants one free roar: canEnter is bypassed once and a flag is saved. The 1.2 s reveal plays, the player clears the wave as the beast, and the form ends with 'The ember sleeps. Earn it back: reach level 3, open Talents (U).' The first tracked quest becomes 'Earn the Roar'. Finally, the play HUD adopts the project's own showcase layout: level and XP fold into the player card with a 4 px XP strip along the hotbar, the quest tracker collapses to the one active objective (expanding on Q or hover), the tool rail auto-hides in combat, and non-critical panels fade after 4 s idle.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Today the first second is a navy void with the wordmark over the mascot's face (menu.png, opened). The tagline promises a block sandbox, and the game's signature moment sits 10 to 20 minutes and three counter quests away, while about a fifth of the play screen is UI (explore-day.png). After this, a stranger sees the game at its best within one second, and a new player is a fire comet clearing a siege within the first minute.

moves.name: A coast that reads as voxel water
moves.what: Move the Ocean's Fresnel, highlight and foam splice from after <dithering_fragment> to just after <opaque_fragment>, so fog and the terrain's aerial haze apply to them. Fade foam and the highlight band by distance from the centre (smoothstep 70 to 105 m), and fade the plane's edge so the far ring takes over; that removes the square corner against the sky. On each recentre, bake a 96x96 byte depth texture from climate.surfaceBlockAt and use it three ways: scale wave amplitude by depth (calm water up to about 3 m deep, the full swell only offshore); draw 3 toon depth bands (turquoise, teal, navy) with a crisp foam line where the depth reaches 0; and aim the Fresnel at the analytic sky colour. Below sea level, add a teal underwater fog, a screen tint and a moving caustic term on the seabed, built the same way as the cloud-shadow hook. Cache oceanVisibleNear per integer cell. Extend the generated wave shader so the physics surface and the drawn surface share the depth-scaled amplitude table.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Every inlet and valley pond runs the same 2 m open-ocean storm swell. Mid-distance water reads as stepped white terraces, and the open sea bulges over the coast as a glossy plastic hump that ends in a visible square corner. Underwater looks like a dry seabed. After this, coasts read as calm turquoise lagoons with a foam line, with deep navy water offshore, and going underwater looks like it.

It holds 3 or 4 variants each of: sword hit on flesh, armour and stone; swing whoosh; block break and place per material (stone, wood, dirt, leaves, sand); footsteps per surface; and pickup. Each play picks a random variant at plus or minus 4% pitch through masterBus. Every hit is layered: the existing synth transient, a recorded body, and a tail scaled by tier (light, heavy, crit). The perfect dodge and the heavy release get their own tails, and recorded bodies go under the dragon roar and the windup voices. Synthesis stays as the fallback while the bank loads. Credit the packs in CreditsScreen. Read the Sonniss GDC licence before using anything from it, because whether it allows files that anyone can download from a web build is unverified.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Every sound effect is a synthesized tone or noise burst (blockBreak is a 150 Hz sawtooth), so hits, steps and breaks have no material and no weight, and audio carries roughly half of impact. After this, a heavy on stone sounds different from a light on flesh, footsteps tell the player what ground they are on, and the perfect dodge has a signature ring.

moves.name: One material grammar
moves.what: Re-author the 16 procedural texture layers as structured bold-flat pixel art, still procedural and free: 2 to 4 clustered tones in low-frequency shapes. Grass gets blade clumps with a lighter top rim; stone gets chunky facets with 1 px cracks; leaves become lit lobes with no black holes; sand gets ripples; wood gets rings on top faces and bark on side faces. Add per-face selection to the terrain shader from the world-space normal: grass and snow side faces sample dirt or stone, with a 3 to 4 texel turf or snow cap taken from fract(vWorldPos.y). Turn TERRAIN_MIPMAPS on; it is built and proven, and the decision now sits within Kevin's grant. Props built with voxelKit (huts, stalls, walls) take the terrain palette through per-face two-tone vertex colour plus the same per-block jitter, and keep their ink outline. Grass: replace the stride-2 lattice and its early-return cap with per-column jittered placement and reservoir sampling, which also removes the bald strip along the +z edge of every chunk. Each tuft becomes a crossed 3-blade tapered shape coloured from root to tip (root = the ground's grass colour times AO, tip = a warm lime), with height and hue jitter, the budget spent by distance ring at the same total count, and one world-level InstancedMesh replacing one per chunk. Motes: fade them within 4 m and beyond 35 m of the camera, remove them against sky, halve their size, gate them by context (forest, dusk, the Hearth, shrines), and replace them with fireflies at night.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Up close every block is per-texel white noise: leaves read as mouldy, black-speckled cubes. Grass hills are green cliffs with no dirt band under the turf. Props use a third render language. Meadows are sparse ticks on a grid with a bald strip, and white orbs float over open sky like dirt on the lens (explore-day.png, hearth.png, opened). After this, terrain, buildings and grass read as one hand-made world.

moves.name: Encounters, and a siege that marches
moves.what: Add a self-contained encounter table in a new game/encounters.js, keyed by zoneTier, biome and day or night. Tier 0 by day is gentle: a lone husk, 3 skitterlings or passives, and no brutes near spawn by day. Tier 1 brings hound packs of 3, which split because flank sides are already hashed, or 2 skeletons screened by a husk. Tier 2 and beyond brings camps: a brute and 2 husks idling around a small stamp until aggro'd. Tier 2+ spawns can carry an 'Ember-touched' elite affix: +60% HP, a rim glow through the existing per-instance rim colour, a burning zone on death through elementZones, and double loot and XP. Health and damage scale with zone tier. Each group spawns around one anchor, within the existing maxMobs caps. Add a siege director in a new game/siegeDirector.js, a scheduler with a 15 Hz bridge. At the horn it picks 1 or 2 bearings, shown as red compass wedges and a horizon glow. Waves spawn at 0, 45 and 95 s from the treeline 40 to 60 m out, drawn from the night-tier table, and head for the nearer of the Hearth and the player's most recent cluster of placed blocks; the worker only needs targetX and targetZ. Wave 3 is led by a named captain elite carrying a banner, whose death ends the siege early with the dawn payoff, and each night N scales wave size and elite count. Add a soft ember cache on death: banked Aspect meters and carried coins drop at the death site, marked on the compass, and touching the cache restores them; dying again first forfeits it. No items or XP are lost.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Today mobs arrive one random pick at a time, 70% hostile by day, with no packs, camps, elites or scaling by distance. The announced 'siege' raises the spawn cap by 4, centred wherever the player stands, and nothing marches on the Hearth or on anything the player built. After this, day is the calm half of the loop and night is a set piece with a direction, a climax and an early win. Walls and lit bases matter because something marches on them.

moves.name: One feedback grammar: mobs and spells read at a glance
moves.what: Mobs: the windup ramps rim strength and the per-instance outline toward danger red while the body keeps its toon shading. The hit flash becomes 60 to 80 ms of white on the lit band plus a white outline, followed by a 3-frame squash. The fresnel rim runs at every tier, coloured by mood (moon-white at night). Each archetype gets 2 or 3 tones of part detail as data: a lighter face or belly plate, darker hands and feet, and one strap or band. Eyes get HDR emissive so they bloom under move 4's threshold. Rigid parts merge into one vertex-coloured geometry per archetype, with only the animated limbs kept separate, which takes a mob from about 31 draws to about 6, with one Outlines per merged mesh. Spells: each element gets a solid saturated core with an ink outline (normal blend, so it reads on any sky), one additive glow shell and a dark secondary (fire smoke, ice mist, arcane void), all scaled up about 1.5x. Impacts get an expanding ground-ring decal, a short-lived scorch or frost decal, 6 to 10 chunky voxel debris cubes from the existing GPU spark system, and a shock ring. The per-projectile and per-impact pointLights are replaced by a pool of 4 always-mounted lights, assigned each frame to the brightest live effects and set to intensity 0 when unused, so the light count never changes.
moves.why_player_feels_it: At exactly the moments that matter, mobs flood into flat salmon or white cut-outs (perfect-dodge-windup.png, opened). At night on low tier they dissolve against dark ground. Spells are pastel confetti that vanish against a bright sky, and each cast changes the light count, which re-links every lit shader program and hitches the frame mid-fight. After this, a telegraph reads at any distance and any hour, a hit feels like contact, and casting never stutters.

moves.name: The lantern: light is the defence
moves.what: Bake light the way Minecraft described at GDC 2026. In the terrain worker, run a sky-light BFS seeded from the column heightmap and a block-light BFS seeded from emissive blocks: levels 0 to 15, minus 1 per face step, blocked by solids, continuous across chunk borders. Pack both into one byte per vertex (4 bits each) and include it in the greedy-merge key, the lesson of the AO fix in 1be94a5c. The terrain shader samples a 16x16 brightness LUT DataTexture that move 4's colour script rewrites whenever the time of day or the boss sky changes. Add a craftable lantern as a full-cube block (id 16, a texture layer in move 9's grammar, a game-icon, a recipe), lit through the parked ore-glow emissive path. Hostiles do not spawn at light 8 or above. Caves, overhangs and interiors finally get darker than open ground.
moves.why_player_feels_it: There is no local light at night: caves, overhangs and interiors get the same ambient light as open ground, and a player cannot light a base. Against move 4's cool night, a lantern throws a warm pool that shows from across a valley, cave mouths fall into real darkness, and lighting a base becomes how the player defends it. This is the thesis made playable: the ember against the dark.

moves.name: The Shadow Dragon earns the climax
moves.what: Rebuild the dragon as a segmented voxel dragon in the bold-flat box vocabulary: a 5-segment neck, a head with a hinged jaw and horn crest, a 6-segment tapering tail, 4 legs, and 3-bone membrane wings that carry the phase glow. Merge it into 1 to 3 draws and animate it procedurally: a travelling sine down the spine, wing bones with lag, and the jaw opening on breath attacks. Put it on the mob rules. The bite and roar get a windupUntil and run through attackPhase. A bossAsTarget adapter in perfectDodgeTargets makes a perfect dodge of the dive-bite stagger it for 1.4 s: its wings fold and it lands, which is Phase 1's melee opening. The roar gets a 900 ms inhale tell (the jaw opens, the throat emissive ramps, playSpatialSound('roar') pitched down), a 9 m radius with falloff, and can be dodged with i-frames. Three heavies inside one stagger knock it down for 3 s, with the riposte multiplier applying. Ground decals replace the per-attack toasts. Add an entrance roar. Each return tier adds one move: a dive-bomb with a ground-shadow telegraph, then a tail sweep. Light the arena like a stage: a cold rim from the moon side, a warm under-light from lava cracks via the parked ore-glow emissive term, fog roughly halved inside the arena radius, a brighter floor, and the boss silhouetted against a brighter band of crimson sky. Generalise the world-clock pause into a scale for a slow-motion ramp (0.15 back to 1 over about 600 ms) on the killing blow, at most one per 10 s.
moves.why_player_feels_it: The climax is a purple box with two dots and stick wings (boss-closeup.png, opened). Its bite and roar give no warning, and the roar has no range check at all (verified at BossEntity.jsx:313-343). Phase 1 orbits out of melee reach, and the fight ignores the perfect dodge and the heavy, the game's two newest skill verbs. The arena floor is an unreadable dark mass. After this, the last fight is the best fight: a creature recognisable from its silhouette, with a read and a skill answer for every attack.

An e2e plants a boss kill and asserts the mob animation delta runs at about 0.15x real time during the ramp, while an ordinary kill does not ramp. Lookbook boss shots in the arena on both tiers, with a solid-black 64 px silhouette check. gpu-cost-probe: the boss takes at most 3 draws.
moves.heat_budget: Fewer draws than today's boxes and sphere eyes. The arena lighting reuses the directional key (rim through the material) and the ore emissive term, adding no dynamic lights. Slow motion costs nothing. Target: boss-fight GPU within +0.3 ms of an ordinary night.
moves.depends_on: Move 5 (windup rules and stance), move 11 (the merged-part pipeline and the edge telegraph), move 4 (bloom on the throat and eyes), and the parked ore emissive for the lava cracks.
moves.win: A boss fight people clip and share: a readable, beautiful dragon that answers the dodge and the heavy, ending in a slow-motion killing blow under a crimson sky.
moves.compose: Move 14's lit shrines strip its HP and remove its tricks, and move 8 gives it a recorded roar. VICTORY already fires as an event (5b1cb802).
moves.door: Tuning the boss against the new combat speed is a balance commitment. Save compatibility (return tiers, kill nights) must survive the new model. The slow-motion scale replaces a boolean pause with a shared clock that other systems will come to rely on.
moves.rails: iPad: merged draws and no new lights. Touch players need move 3's heavy hold for knockdowns. Arena fog and grade are set per tier.
moves.threat: A procedural spine with many segments can cost main-thread time; animate it in one useFrame over arrays. A dodgeable roar can make phase 2 trivial, so the radius and inhale get tuned in playtests. Overused slow motion reads as lag; cap it at one ramp per 10 s, on climactic beats only.

moves.name: Relight the frontier
moves.what: 'Light the shrine': pressing G at a shrine starts a 45 s hold-the-light event, two waves from move 10's encounter table at that shrine's tier, with the defence radius shown as a ring. Success lights a beam (the landmark emissive plus HDR bloom, and a block-light source once move 12 lands) and increments a saved shrinesLit count. Each lit shrine, up to 3, strips 10% of the dragon's HP and removes one of its tricks, announced on the compass; unlit shrines show dim. Dungeons get what they lack: a dungeonSites(cx, cz) helper built from the worker's hash (the shrines.js pattern), an altar chest tier-boosted like shrine chests in place of the sand 'Treasure block', and a guardian group (elite at tier 1+) on entry. Discovered dungeons stay on the minimap. Quests become an authored 6-beat spine, given and handed in with G on the NPCs through a bold-flat Modal dialogue card: Pike, survive the prologue; Mara, forge a stone sword from mined stone; Wren, hold the Hearth through the first siege; Pike, light the first shrine; Bram, kill the camp captain; Pike, the Blight Heart. Counter quests survive as optional bounties on Bram's board, and quest mob names come from MOB_TYPES displayName.
moves.why_player_feels_it: Old Pike says every reclaimed shrine weakens the Blight Heart, and nothing implements it. Dungeons are empty stone rooms. Quests are counters handed out in list order, including 'Defeat 10 zombies' for a mob the game calls Husk, and the NPC 'givers' say one fixed line. After this, exploration has a ladder that leads to the climax and makes it fairer, and the people of the Hearth tell the story.

moves.lived_proof: A unit on bossTierStats with shrinesLit. A unit that dungeonSites matches the worker's isDungeonChunk over a seeded grid. An e2e completes a shrine event and asserts the dragon spawns with less HP; the control is a failed event (the player leaves the radius), which changes nothing. An e2e teleports into a dungeon chunk and asserts a chest exists and the guardians aggro. An e2e completes beat 1 and receives beat 2 only after pressing G on Mara. A unit asserts that quest offering reads the chain order from one source.
moves.heat_budget: About zero GPU: beams reuse the landmark emissive, events spawn within the existing caps, and dialogue is DOM.
moves.depends_on: Move 10 (encounter table for the waves and guardians), move 13 (the dragon's HP and trick hooks) and move 6 (the prologue as beat 1). Move 12 is optional, to make shrines light sources.
moves.win: A frontier the player reclaims shrine by shrine, each beam visible from the Hearth at night, and each one a measurable step toward a dragon they can now beat on their own terms.
moves.compose: Lit beams are the brightest things in move 4's night. The spine walks the player through moves 5, 10 and 13 in order, and gives mining a purpose (Mara's sword).
moves.door: shrinesLit and the quest-chain state enter saves. Old saves need defaults: no shrines lit, and the spine starting at the beat their progress implies.
moves.rails: Touch: G needs a touch affordance, an interact button that appears near NPCs and shrines. The bold-flat Modal must work at iPad sizes. No GPU cost.
moves.threat: A spine that gates the sandbox: beats should guide and never lock the world. Quest text needs zh-CN strings (P5), or the i18n ratchet goes red. A defence event can fail invisibly when knockback carries the player out of the radius, which the ring guards against.

Runtime changes to renderDistance and the far-field radius on coarse-pointer devices: remove them from the governor's steps and set them once at boot. They remesh and remount mid-play on the rail least able to afford it.
The isWebGLContextLost flag is written (useGameStore.jsx:127-128) and read nowhere. Give it its reader in move 1, or delete the dead state.

The global HueSaturation +0.30 on an already saturated palette, and the Bloom luminanceThreshold of 0.65 that blooms the whole sky (GameScene.jsx:117-124). Replace them with a per-mood split-tone and a threshold above 1.0.
Per-projectile and per-impact pointLights in frontend/src/render/spellVfx.jsx:434 and :618: each changes the light count and re-links every lit shader mid-fight. Replace them with a fixed pool of 4.
Daytime motes over open sky: the camera-following 46x26x46 m box at 140 motes on high, including the glare blob beside the crosshair. Gate motes to context and use fireflies at night.
The boss's per-attack text toasts ('Pushed back! Shadow Dragon unleashed a KNOCKBACK ROAR!' and one per fireball) and the roar's range-free hit. Telegraphs become ground decals and an inhale tell.

The title's 0-to-86% black scrim, the hardcoded tagline 'Build • Craft • Cast Spells • Explore' at MenuSystem.jsx:295 (English only, not in i18n), and the title's second antialiased alpha WebGL context rendering while the game canvas also draws behind it.
The floating Level/XP card at bottom centre (SimpleExperienceSystem.jsx:165), right where approaching mobs appear. Fold it into the player card and an XP strip on the hotbar.
The compass's full-text markers that overprint the cardinal letters, and its per-frame innerHTML rebuild. Use icon markers in a persistent node pool, with text only on the active objective.

The opening counter-quest ladder ('place 20 blocks', 'Defeat 10 zombies', 'Defeat 25 skeletons') as the first thing a player sees, and the mob-name mismatches. Counters become optional bounties on Bram's board.
Implementation dev-speak in player-facing talent text, e.g. 'read at the duration timer, not the stat-fold' (visible in progression-open.png).
The dungeon's sand 'Treasure block' on a snow 'marble' altar (terrain.worker.js:224), a reward that is not one. Replace it with a real chest and guardians.
WeatherSystem's per-frame zero-scale matrix writes and buffer re-uploads for 400 rain, 200 snow and the firefly instances in clear weather, plus three empty draws.
SpatialAudioController's per-frame setTargetAtTime writes on unchanged targets and its per-frame occlusion rays.
One drei Outlines mesh per mob part (about 19 per mob, MobModel.jsx:279-349). Use one per merged mesh, and let only body and head cast shadows.
The stride-2 grass lattice with an early-return cap (grassField.js:46-58), which leaves a bald strip along every all-grass chunk, and the one InstancedMesh per chunk.
Accepting looks on SwiftShader capture frames. The 31 baselines remain a regression oracle; looks acceptance moves to the real-GPU, motion-on lookbook, which includes iPad viewports.

A WebGPU/TSL migration: do not start it. Record the decision in DECISIONS.md and revisit when R3F v10 is stable and Safari 27.x has shipped two point releases without a WebGPU regression. Write new shader terms as small pure GLSL modules with JS mirrors (the leafFeel.js and oreGlow.js pattern) so a later port is mechanical.

Candidate for the next tranche, not cut blind: the fire-and-ice annihilation rule in elementZones.js:16-22, where combining two elements erases both. It punishes the Elemancer fantasy and should become a reaction table (steam that cancels windups).
sequencing:
Phase 0: deliver what is built, and open the eyes. Finish T1/T2 and the T3 green receipt, then push, so the memo'd post chain, the 60 fps cap and the shadow reset reach the live site Kevin tested. Ask Kevin for his iPadOS and Safari version. Build move 1's instruments before any fix: the Diagnostics panel, ipad-probe on the production build in WebKit at both iPad viewports, the lookbook contact sheet, and the powermetrics A/B script that Kevin runs. Take a BEFORE set with them. Apply the parked wip/perf-t3-features work by file group, since canvasPace, the compass dedupe and the ore emissive are inputs to moves 1, 2, 12 and 13. Then run moves 1 and 2 as two lanes on mostly disjoint files (GameScene/FrameCap/quality/TitleDiorama against Atmosphere shadows/HUD/Weather/SpatialAudio). Kevin's milestone ultrareview runs on that state, before it is pushed.

Phase 1: the core feel and look, in three disjoint lanes. Move 3 (TouchControls), move 4 (mood/Atmosphere/skyDome/Terrain lights patch/post grade) and move 5 (locomotion, a new combatStance, ai.worker, mobArchetypes, DamageDirection). Move 4 lands together with the owed 147-to-151 re-baseline as one Baseline-Review commit kept separate from src, because both rewrite all 31 frames.

Phase 2: first impression and surfaces. Move 6 follows moves 3, 4 and 5. Moves 7 (Ocean) and 9 (proceduralTextures/Terrain/grass/motes) run in parallel, with one combined re-baseline. Move 8 (sound) starts as a standing parallel lane once move 5's verbs settle.

Phase 3: the threat layer, built sequentially because each move feeds the next. Move 11 first (its merged mob pipeline and light pool are prerequisites), then move 10 (encounters and siege), then move 12 (lantern; needs move 4's night, the ore emissive and move 10's siege), then move 13 (dragon; needs moves 5 and 11), then move 14 (needs move 10's table and move 13's HP hooks). Build order therefore differs from rank, which is impact per cost.

Platform: after phase 1's re-baseline, bump three to r186, R3F to 9.8.2 and @react-three/postprocessing to 3.2.2 together. Pin shadows="percentage" first and diagnose the r174 sky saturation with a sky-only A/B. The bump replaces move 1's local composer setSize and effect wrappers, and needs one combined re-baseline. A SunLight CSM trial follows it.

Discipline for every move: its own plan doc in docs/superpowers/plans/ before building; red-first gates; real-input e2e; a mutate-e2e batch with an identity mutant; lookbook frames opened by eye; a fresh /code-review xhigh per change range; and a heat check against move 2's budget before landing. That budget is at most 6 ms of GPU per frame at high on the M3 Max under the 60 cap, GPU power at least 40% below today's live build, and on iPad at most 1 tier change per minute after warm-up. These are targets until the instruments measure them.

Next tranche after these 14: the beast form held in third person for its full 14 s (Kevin's recorded third-person direction, scoped to a 14 s window), capstones that change verbs instead of adding stats, an element reaction table, and gamepad support with rebinding.
